wu: Warm-up: 'Food Categories Race'. Teacher writes 4 columns on the board: Fruit, Vegetables, Drinks, Other. Students in teams take turns running to the board and writing one food word per category. Fastest team with correct words wins.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'I Spy with My Little Eye' - Teacher says 'I spy something you eat for breakfast', students guess using 'Is it...?'
Alternative 2: 'Mime the Food' - Students mime a food/drink, others guess 'Are you eating/drinking...?'
pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of Thanksgiving foods (turkey, pumpkin pie, potatoes, cranberry sauce). Model: 'How many potatoes?' 'Some potatoes.' 'How much cranberry sauce?' 'Some cranberry sauce.' Elicit countable/uncountable. Check with thumbs up/down: 'Is potato countable?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use realia (apple, bread, milk) to demonstrate countable/uncountable.
Alternative 2: Draw a simple market scene on the board and ask 'How much...? How many...?'
prac: Guided practice: 'Shopping List Relay'. Teams get a list with gaps (e.g., '___ apples, ___ milk'). One student runs to the board, writes 'some' or 'any', then next student adds the word. Teacher monitors for accuracy.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Fill in the Blanks' worksheet with pictures of food, students write 'some/any'.
Alternative 2: 'Pair Drill' - Student A asks 'How many...?', Student B answers 'Some.../Any...?'
ls: Listening slot: Play a short dialogue between two friends planning a Thanksgiving meal. Students listen and circle 'some' or 'any' on their worksheet (e.g., 'Do we have ___ potatoes?').
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up If You Like...'. Teacher calls out foods (e.g., 'Stand up if you like pizza!'), students stand and say 'I like some pizza!' or 'I don't like any pizza!'
prod: Production task: 'Thanksgiving vs. Moroccan Harvest Survey'. Students in pairs interview 3 classmates: 'What food do you eat for Eid al-Adha? How much...? How many...?' They graph results and present to the class.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text about a typical Thanksgiving meal. They underline all countable nouns. Then, they write 3 sentences about their family's meal using 'some/any'.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'Thanksgiving Food Song' (tune: 'Frère Jacques'). Close with: 'Today we learned to ask about quantities with How much/How many and some/any. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams write food words in columns: Fruit, Vegetables, Drinks, Other.
Teams fill gaps with 'some/any' and food words on the board.
Students stand and say 'I like some...' when a food is called.
Interview classmates about Eid al-Adha food and graph results.
Students sort picture cards into countable/uncountable piles.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 more sentences about their ideal Thanksgiving meal.
Support: Use a word bank with 'some/any' and food words for the writing task.
hw: Homework 1: Complete a 10-item worksheet on countable/uncountable nouns.
Homework 2: Interview 3 people: 'What are you thankful for?' and report back.
Homework 3: Write a short paragraph about your family's favorite food using 'some/any'.
tip: Teach 'some/any' through visual aids (full/empty containers) to make the abstract concept concrete for beginners. Connect to Moroccan harvest customs to build cultural relevance.
